items.title: Native refuses a `map` closure that calls a function returning `any` - unbound generic parameter of `map`
items.body: Found by lane db-58. A closure passed to `map` whose body calls a function returning `any` is refused natively as "unbound generic type parameter (parameter 1 of `map`)"; the JS backend builds it. Repro: `scripts/integration/sweeps/order58/repros/repro-map-closure-returning-any.vl`. std::db works around it with a `for`/`push` loop; remove that when this is fixed. Size S-M.

items.title: std::db: node binds every number as REAL, native binds integers as INTEGER - an untyped column stores 7.0 vs 7
items.body: Found by lane db-58 and documented in native.md. A column with no declared type stores `7` as `7.0` on JS and as INTEGER natively, because node's sqlite binds every JS number as a REAL. A possible fix: the integer `SqlValue` impls pass a BigInt on JS. Columns with a declared INTEGER affinity are unaffected. Size S.

items.title: Native ws client: no size cap on a received message, and the address lookup cannot be cancelled
items.body: Left by lane ws-58, noted in `crates/vilan-rt/src/ws.rs`. (1) The client accepts a frame or a fragmented message of any size; give it a cap with a close code 1009, matching what the server side does. (2) The address lookup and connect run on a helper thread; `close()` abandons the result but the lookup itself runs to its own timeout. Size S each.

items.title: Owner question: should a backed enum implement `SqlValue` automatically, as it gets `Hashable`?
items.body: M175 made bind lists `List<dyn SqlValue>`. A string-backed enum (kolt's `Role`) no longer binds: four kolt sites need `.value()`. Node used to bind the enum as its string; natively it never built. Options: (a) backed enums get a `SqlValue` impl automatically, bound as their backing value; (b) leave it explicit (`role.value()`), the shipped state. Recommendation: (b) for now; a derive (`[derive(SqlValue)]`) is the lighter door if the sites multiply.
